items.title: Euro FX futures rebound above 1.12 as volatility edges higher.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures surged back above 1.12 on Thursday, reversing off a new year-to-date low near 1.11 set in the prior session. The currency rebounded as the U.S. dollar weakened, though the CVOL index showed volatility edging higher despite the price recovery. Markets face potential weekend event risks involving Middle East tensions and European sovereign debt, while immediate focus turns to Fed Chair Warsh speaking in Bangkok and Friday's release of the New York Fed Services Index and industrial production data.

items.title: Flight to quality hits tech stocks.
items.excerpt: U.S. equities are mixed with tech stocks weighing on the S P 500 and Nasdaq-100, while the Dow and Russell hold up better. A flight to quality pushes Treasury yields lower as investors pull back from AI-related tech momentum to seek predictable income. In commodities, gold, silver and crude oil push higher, while copper and bitcoin drop. Markets look ahead to Federal Reserve speakers Kevin Warsh and Beth Hammack for any signal on inflation and interest rates before the next FOMC meeting. Plus, a look at the $1 billion market cap earnings slate and incoming Eurozone CPI and U.S. industrial production data.

items.title: Euro futures hit 17-month low as U.S. inflation tops expectations.
items.excerpt: Euro futures drop to a 17-month low as a divergence in U.S. and European inflation data reshapes interest rate expectations. Bob Iaccino unpacks the market reaction after U.S. core inflation rose 2.6%, keeping the possibility of a late-October Fed rate hike in the conversation. Meanwhile, German inflation held steady at 3.3%, reinforcing market expectations that the European Central Bank will leave rates unchanged despite President Lagarde's warnings on energy prices. Iaccino highlights the downside momentum for the euro as the stronger U.S. economic data adds pressure across the currency complex.

items.title: Euro futures rally from 18-month lows on dovish Fed remarks.
items.excerpt: Euro futures reversed early weakness to finish higher on Tuesday, bouncing from an 18-month low near 1.1150 to close around 1.1200. The rally was sparked by a softening U.S. dollar, following dovish remarks from New York Fed President John Williams suggesting a less aggressive stance on 2027 rate hikes. Meanwhile, FX volatility continues to ease, with the CVOL index extending its slow decline from the October 1 peak. Despite the daily bounce, fund positioning remains heavily bearish, as speculators increased their net short positions to the highest level since February 2020.

items.title: Canadian Dollar futures hit 18-month low on weak jobs report.
items.excerpt: Canadian Dollar futures fell to an 18-month low as unexpected job losses in Canada weighed on market sentiment. Statistics Canada reported September employment dropped by 68,300, defying expectations for a gain of 9,200, while the unemployment rate climbed to 6.5%. Labor force participation declined to 64.8%, its lowest level since 1997 outside of the pandemic. The weak labor market data pushed back Bank of Canada rate hike expectations, with money markets pricing out an October rate increase. Meanwhile, CME Group's FedWatch Tool indicates higher probability for a December FOMC rate hike in the U.S., creating a divergence in monetary policy outlooks that continues to exert downward pressure on the Canadian dollar.
